statement: Less than two years after Hudaybiyyah, Banu Bakr (allies of Quraysh) attacked Khuza'ah (allies of the Muslims) at night at a watering place, aided by men of Quraysh.
Ibn Abbas: he set out in Ramadan with ten thousand, in the eighth year after coming to Madinah.
notes: Number from memory; not machine-checked. The narration says 'eight and a half years after his arrival in Madinah'.

statement: He concealed the destination so Quraysh would be surprised and fighting in the sanctuary avoided.
notes: The interception of Hatib's letter (Bukhari 4274, machine-checked) shows the secrecy.

statement: At Marr az-Zahran fires were lit; Abu Sufyan, Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl came out for news, saw fires 'like the fires of Arafah', were caught by guards and brought to the Prophet; Abu Sufyan accepted Islam.
notes: Machine-checked. That every man lit a fire by his order is from the Seerah.

statement: Al-Abbas held Abu Sufyan where the army passed; tribes passed; the Ansar under Sa'd ibn Ubadah; Sa'd said 'today is the day of slaughter, today the Ka'bah's sanctity will be made lawful'; the Prophet said Sa'd was wrong, that this was a day Allah would exalt the Ka'bah and it would be clothed.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against the full text ('kadhaba Sa'd', rendered 'has spoken wrongly').

statement: He declared: whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe, whoever lays down arms is safe, whoever shuts his door is safe.
notes: Direct speech. The Muslim dataset has the narration of Abu Hurayrah (no. 4622); wording from memory; Abd al-Baqi number from memory.

statement: He entered from the upper side of Makkah, eight years after leaving; there was little fighting.
notes: Machine-checked (he entered from Kuda; two of Khalid's horsemen were killed). The narration script omits the clash at Khalid's entrance.

statement: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal saw him on his camel on the day of the conquest reciting Surah al-Fath.
He entered with his head bowed in humility until his beard nearly touched the saddle.
Ibn Mas'ud: there were 360 idols around the Ka'bah; he struck them with a stick saying 'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished; truth has come and falsehood neither originates nor restores'.
He refused to enter the Ka'bah until the images inside were removed, then entered and said the takbir in its corners.
notes: Number from memory (Ibn Abbas); not machine-checked.

statement: The report 'Go, for you are free' (idhhabu fa-antum at-tulaqa') has a weak chain.
notes: Editorial statement. From Ibn Ishaq without a connected chain; graded da'if by al-Albani (from memory). Reviewer to confirm.

statement: He honoured the safety he had granted; the Makkans became known as at-Tulaqa'.
notes: Bukhari 4337 (machine-checked) uses the term 'at-Tulaqa' for them at Hunayn. A small number of named individuals were excluded from the amnesty, most of whom were later pardoned; not narrated. Reviewer to decide whether 'no vengeance' needs qualifying.

statement: Abu Shurayh: on the day after the conquest he said Allah, not the people, made Makkah sacred; no believer may shed blood or cut a tree there; it was permitted to him only for an hour of a day; its sanctity has returned; let the present inform the absent.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the first part.
Paraphrase of meaning. The surah's time of revelation is discussed by scholars; the script says only that it 'speaks of that time'.
